words.meaning: First aorist active indicative of diaskorpizw, a somewhat rare verb, the very opposite of "gathered together" (sunagogwn). More exactly he scattered his property. It is the word used of winnowing grain (Matthew 25:24). The idea is throwing it away.
words.plain: Wasted [Greek: dieskorpisen] literally means to scatter — like grain thrown to the wind [the same word used for winnowing grain in Matthew 25:24]. The son didn't just spend his money; he dispersed it in all directions, carelessly and completely. It's the opposite of gathering, the opposite of stewardship.

words.meaning: Sandals, "bound under." Both sandals and ring are marks of the freeman as slaves were barefooted. (Robertson's NT Word Pictures)
words.plain: Shoes [Greek: hypodema, sandals, literally 'bound under'] — sandals were a mark of freedom. Slaves went barefoot. By putting shoes on his son's feet, the father declares publicly: this person is not a servant in my house. He is a son — fully restored.

words.meaning: Imperfect tense. It expressed a necessity in the father’s heart and in the joy of the return that justifies the feasting. (Robertson's NT Word Pictures)
words.plain: It was meet [Greek: edei — 'it was necessary']. Not a choice — a necessity. The father isn't defending himself; he's explaining what joy requires. When someone who was dead is alive again, when someone who was lost is found, celebration is not optional. It's the only fitting response.
